2.00.betting_forecast: Evs Adaay Of Scarlett, 2/1 Dance A Jig, 100/30 A Bear Affair, 16/1 Crusherman.
2.00.spotlight_verdict: Adaay Of Scarlett didn't half look good at Newmarket and his connections already have eyes on the Royal meeting. However, from where he was early doors, DANCE A JIG did well to bustle up A Bear Affair in the Brocklesby and improvement would appear a formality. The same can be said of the winner, though he carries a penalty. Crusherman isn't dismissed by any means when his yard's juveniles are renowned for stepping up on their debut form, and it looked a good race at Newbury.[Alistair Jones]

horses.spotlight_comment: 9-2 chance when fending off Dance A Jig by just under a length in the Brocklesby at Doncaster (5f, good to soft); showed a good attitude and the Hannon youngsters often improve with racing, but he does have to concede 3lb to the runner-up whose effort was a tad more eyecatching.

Mehmas colt who cost 110,000euros as a yearling; strong in the betting (11-8) and strong in the finish when completely dominating a 5f novice at Newmarket's Craven meeting (5f, good); Royal Ascot was talked about afterwards and this colt looks well above average already.

9-2 chance when fending off Dance A Jig by just under a length in the Brocklesby at Doncaster (5f, good to soft); showed a good attitude and the Hannon youngsters often improve with racing, but he does have to concede 3lb to the runner-up whose effort was a tad more eyecatching.

52,000euros yearling; it looked a deep Newbury 5f maiden (good) in which he was beaten just over 3l and after racing prominently inexperience was evident when push came to shove; it was an encouraging start and juveniles from this yard are renowned for improving on their debut efforts.

Home-bred 2yo who hails from a well-established sprinting family; got behind early in the Brocklesby (5f, good to soft; 6-1) but made up a significant amount of ground to give A Bear Affair something to think about; should be all the wiser this time and he's 3lb better off with the winner.

2.35.betting_forecast: 2/1 Sweet William, 7/2 Caballo De Mar, 9/2 Tarriance, 5/1 Tabletalk, 12/1 Miss Alpilles, 16/1 Ascending, Beylerbeyi, Dubai Future,
2.35.spotlight_verdict: The thoroughly tried-and-tested option is Sweet William who comes up short against the top stayers but regularly emerges in front when his sights are slightly lowered, as they are today. If making his first start of the season proves a slight chink in his armour, however, the one to take advantage may be TABLETALK who produced a big run in Saudi Arabia 11 weeks ago and is now much better off at the weights with the promising Tarriance who finished just behind him. Caballo De Mar found only one too good in the Dubai Gold Cup in March, but Dubai Future was 15l adrift, having won that race in 2025.[Richard Austen]

horses.spotlight_comment: Landed the Cork Derby (1m4f) last May and a Royal Ascot handicap (2m4f) last June, before his excellent second in the Ebor Handicap at York (1m6f) in August; not disgraced on final start but needs a serious advance to mix it with the best of these in today's Group 3.

Won the 2m2f Cesarewitch in October and has run well in defeat on AW in his four starts (1m2f, 1m3f and 2m) this January-April; keeps catching the eye with his late gains from off the pace and might still have more to give, but today's move out of handicaps certainly requires it.

Much improved last year, best effort to land the Group 1 Cadran at Longchamp (2m4f, soft) in October; close second in the Dubai Gold Cup at Meydan (2m, good) was a fine start to this campaign and his run on good to firm at Royal Ascot last June, although subsequently eclipsed, looked excellent at the time; needs respect but concedes weight all round.
horses.breeding: b g Phoenix Of Spain - Oberyn

horses.spotlight_comment: A novice event remains his only win from ten races but he was fourth in the 2024 Derby and St Leger; well held in Saudi Arabia and Dubai on his only two starts last year, left Owen Burrows for 16,000gns last October and gelded last month; some caution has to be advised.

Has delivered smart efforts almost every season since 2020 (missed 2024) and last year's win in the 2m Dubai Gold Cup at Meydan was one of his best; that campaign went the wrong way and he did not perk up when returning for Dubai Gold Cup (20-1) five weeks ago, but holds a cracking chance if returning to his best.

Won 1m6f handicap at Goodwood (good to firm) last August and a first crack at 2m suited her even better when she led over 1f out to score at 20-1 in a Listed race at Newmarket (good) in September; today's Group 3 should demand plenty more but she could still have untapped potential at 2m+.
horses.breeding: b m Sea The Stars - Alma Linda

horses.spotlight_comment: Headgear and Rab Havlin all starts; not straightforward but he nearly always gives his running, including at this track; he did not have the top stayers to worry about last September when winning his second Doncaster Cup and the same seems to apply today, so he's a leading player.
horses.breeding: b g Sea The Stars - Gale Force

horses.spotlight_comment: No win since Melrose Handicap at York (1m6f, good to firm) in 2024 but he ran very well in 1m4f Group races on first three starts last season and returned to that form when a close second in Saudi Arabia (1m7f) 11 weeks ago; that puts him back in the picture even though he's unraced over this far.

Won the Melrose Handicap at York (1m6f, good to firm) last August, before the St Leger proved too tough; gelded soon after and ran well when third in Saudi Arabia (1m7f) in February; runner-up Tabletalk conceded him 11lb that day and it's only 1lb today, but this 4yo should retain potential for 2m+.

3.10.betting_forecast: 11/8 Wise Approach, 7/2 Brussels, 4/1 Coppull, 8/1 Ghost Mode, 12/1 Ardisia, Division, 25/1 Crown Relic, 33/1 Midnight Tango.
3.10.spotlight_verdict: The Middle Park 1-2-3 Wise Approach (second choice), Brussels and Coppull lock horns again and it could be that the Godolphin runner confirms his superiority despite having to concede weight all round. While they have been plying their trade in Group 1 company, it is a runner who comes here on the back of an AW handicap success who is arguably the most interesting contender. GHOST MODE did a lot wrong at Southwell seven weeks ago but he still won in a manner rarely seen in competitive sprint handicaps and the market support for him suggested it wasn't a surprise. He will need to keep straighter today but he looked a Group horse in waiting at Southwell and the fact his trainer is prepared to risk a most-appealing handicap mark to come here looks significant.[Paul Smith]

horses.spotlight_comment: Progressive as a 2yo, winning five times and also second of 11 in the 2yo race over C&D on Champions Day; should appreciate the return to a stiff 6f having weakened over 7f in the Greenham two weeks ago; one to consider.

Won a 6f maiden at the Curragh on debut before a string of good efforts in defeat in good races, notably second-place finishes in the Middle Park (0.75l behind Wise Approach and 5lb better off) and the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf Sprint; should be in the shake-up.
horses.breeding: b c Wootton Bassett - Fond Words

horses.spotlight_comment: All races at 7f, winning a maiden and a novice at Wolverhampton in good style before his creditable fifth in a Deauville Group 3 last month (good to soft); drops in trip with a tongue-tie added for a trainer who this in 2020 and 2023.

Promise on good to firm on debut; won his next three starts, two novice events and a York Listed race, before pulling his chance away over C&D on Champions Day; improvement required now upped to a Group 3 but he's in excellent hands and still has some potential.

Five runs as a 2yo; made debut over 6f but campaigned at 7f afterwards, running away with a maiden at Chester (good to soft) before a good second in a York sales race last October; absent for five months prior to a facile success in a 6f handicap at Southwell in March, racing freely and hanging left in the straight but in a different class to some fair handicappers; in much deeper today and looks to face a stiff task at the weights but the Southwell performance smacked of a hugely talented, if slightly wayward, colt and this stiff 6f should suit; unraced on faster than good.

Ran well in Listed/Group 3 company last summer following her maiden win at Hamilton and her two lesser efforts at the end of the campaign can both be excused; this free-going filly shouldn't mind the return to sprinting but she will need to raise her game a notch.
horses.breeding: b f Night Of Thunder - Nina Bailarina

horses.spotlight_comment: On the up when last seen, rounding off his 2yo campaign with a comfortable come-from-behind win in the Middle Park in September (6f, good to firm); may confirm his superiority over Brussels and Coppull despite the weights turnaround and he is not fully exposed just yet.

3.45.betting_forecast: 7/2 Jonquil, 4/1 Remmooz, 11/2 Rashabar, 6/1 Holloway Boy, 7/1 Bowmark, Chancellor, 8/1 La Botte, 14/1 Seacruiser, 16/1
3.45.spotlight_verdict: Jonquil (second choice) and Holloway Boy set the standard but further progress from REMMOOZ (nap) looks assured this season. The Owen Burrows-trained selection had only just made his debut this time last year but ended that campaign with a Listed win and is now within striking distance of Group-race success. The others provide stacks of interest too.[Richard Austen]

horses.spotlight_comment: Lightly raced 4yo from top yard; headstrong up front in the Group 1 Prix du Jockey Club (10.5f) last June and also failed to settle when held up in York Group 3 (1m1f) last August on his only subsequent start; returns to 1m for reappearance but whether he's calmed down after being gelded may be the key.

Had wind surgery last May and gelded last June; returned to action with five races in November-April which left his turf form way behind, particularly those at 1m; ran respectably in first-time cheekpieces on latest outing; player on that AW form but return to turf asks a question.

His strike-rate is an unimpressive 3-26 but he's seldom far away and last October's excellent second in a top handicap over C&D preceded an AW Listed win; came up short at Doha and Meydan early this year but showed enough to suggest he should be on the premises.

2025 seemed to establish that he's better over 1m than 6f or 7f and the best of those efforts, including at the top level, give him a good chance in today's company; reappearance in Abu Dhabi in February was not of the same order but he could bounce back.
horses.breeding: b c Lope De Vega - Jovial

horses.spotlight_comment: Went close in the Britannia at Royal Ascot (1m, good to firm) last June on his fourth start; not seen again until a good fourth at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW) this March, despite a slow start and having to come very wide in the straight; disappointing favourite in the Lincoln at Doncaster three weeks later, perhaps with the good to soft ground against him but overall improvement is required moving from handicaps into this Group 3.
horses.breeding: b c Too Darn Hot - Panmolle

horses.spotlight_comment: Has raced as far as 2m1f in 2024 and never shorter than 1m2f; third at last year's Royal Ascot came over 1m4f but he broke a losing sequence when diverted from top handicaps to a 1m2f Listed race at Goodwood last September; the prospect of 1m now doesn't seem so ridiculous but a career best is needed.

Group 3 Jersey at Royal Ascot last June was the only time he's failed to improve his rating in six-race career but even then he managed fourth of 15; close third in handicap at York Ebor meeting (1m, good to firm) preceded win number four in a 7f Listed race at Newbury; while better is needed in this Group 3, he looks the type to find it in this second season.
horses.breeding: b c Blue Point - Lady Ramon

horses.spotlight_comment: Looked a good prospect when making all in a 1m Newmarket maiden (good to soft) in September 2024; reappeared only three weeks ago but made eye-catching late gains to finish a close third in that strong conditions stakes at Thirsk (7f, good; 12-1); this race demands far more but return to 1m (he looks bred for further still) will help and he should be capable of better.
horses.breeding: b g Sea The Stars - Crimean Queen

4.20.betting_forecast: 6/1 Artagnan, 7/1 Pixie Diva, 8/1 Combustion, 9/1 Hockney, 10/1 Another Abbot, Duran, Mesaafi, Rage Of Thunder, 12/1 All
4.20.spotlight_verdict: A competitive sprint with the best pace appearing to be up the middle of the track. Further progress from Combustion can't be ruled out, while Existent and Duran are likely to be suited by the demands of this test. Pixie Diva did enough at Yarmouth last month to think she was still in top form but FAR ABOVE THE LAW could be the answer. His first run for his new stable was promising and he looks well treated on the pick of last year's efforts for Alice Haynes.[Paul Smith]

horses.spotlight_comment: Second of 16 in a C&D handicap last September; followed that with a good run at Haydock but he went up the weights and was well beaten at Lingfield when last seen; ran well after an absence last year but perhaps a shade high in the weights for this.
horses.breeding: b g Cable Bay - Go Glamorous

horses.spotlight_comment: Effective at 5f but last summer's two wins came over 6f; not beaten far at Chelmsford (5f) when last seen in December; still has relatively low mileage.
horses.breeding: b g Harry Angel - Huma Bird

horses.spotlight_comment: Two solid placed efforts have followed his AW win (6f; dead-heated) at Chelmsford last October; still has relatively low mileage and a promising claimer has been booked; first 5f run since his 2yo days.

His first three starts saw him well beaten over 7f but he has not looked back since dropped to 6f, winning seven times and placed on his other three runs; could only manage second at Chelmsford five weeks ago but the horse to beat him is now rated 17lb higher and that shouldn't be used as evidence he is in the handicapper's grip; more to prove back on turf and at a new trip but few arrive in better form.

Second in this race last year before running out the ready winner of a 5f AW handicap at Haydock last May (good to firm) off a 1lb lower mark; made an encouraging return to action at Beverley 16 days ago; each-way shout.
Made a winning debut for this yard at Newmarket last July (5f, good to firm) and he is now 3lb lower; patchy record since but he can go well fresh and he has a good C&D run on his record.
horses.breeding: b g Holy Roman Emperor - Aspasias Tizzy

horses.spotlight_comment: Well handicapped on his best form for Alice Haynes and he made an encouraging stable debut when a close third at Southwell three weeks ago; one to be interested in.
horses.breeding: b g Far Above - Cindy Bear

horses.spotlight_comment: Both wins and most of his best RPRs have come on AW but his turf runs have come in stronger company than this; drops to 5f for the first time in his career; others look safer.
horses.breeding: b g Hello Youmzain - Sailor Moon

horses.spotlight_comment: Down the field in three maiden/novice runs but he proved a different proposition on his handicap debut last September (6f, AW; first run after wind surgery), landing a gamble in emphatic fashion; followed up, again easily, in a selling handicap at Thirsk one week later; came up short off his revised mark at Newcastle five weeks ago (first run for 193 days); better than that but dropping to 5f asks a new question of him.
Ran quite well when an unconsidered 100-1 shot at Royal Ascot last summer but that didn't prove a springboard to better things; down in the weights but best watched back from a 245-day break.
horses.breeding: b g Dandy Man - Play Mate

horses.spotlight_comment: Not handicapped out of things and his latest run at Pontefract, his first start for 12 weeks, was creditable; twice a course winner and likely to make a bold bid.
horses.breeding: b g Lethal Force - Little Nymph

horses.spotlight_comment: Ran a fine race when third over C&D last July and he turns up here off an 8lb lower mark; poorly drawn when down the field at Lingfield on Good Friday; could bounce back with a big run.
horses.breeding: b g Exceed And Excel - Romaana

horses.spotlight_comment: Narrow Newcastle win on her penultimate start; did best of the rest behind an emphatic all-the-way winner at Yarmouth three weeks ago (5f, good); this race should be more conventional and she is more appealing than many.

Not without his quirks but he has plenty of ability for one of his rating and everything clicked in a Class 6 handicap at Salisbury last June (6f, good to firm); three second placings followed and he should win more races this year; the drop back to 5f for this habitual slow-starter is a concern though.
horses.breeding: b g Inns Of Court - Stormy Clouds

horses.spotlight_comment: The winner of five AW handicaps (5f-6f) since September for her new stable; 6lb higher than for the latest of them and others appeal as being better treated.

4.55.betting_forecast: Evs So Regal, 7/2 Crownright, 9/2 Lyrics Of Life, 10/1 Gesayed, 12/1 Light Dreamer, 14/1 Machadadorp, 20/1 Annastarzy.
4.55.spotlight_verdict: When considering that SO REGAL looked decidedly green and yet still needed no more than hands and heels encouragement from Ryan Moore to see off Lyrics Of Life at Newmarket, the Gosden filly smacks of a filly with Pattern-race potential. Lyrics Of Life could again be her principal danger armed with a 6lb pull. Gesayed and Crownright are no doubt capable of better.[Alistair Jones]

horses.spotlight_comment: Confined to 1m last season and probably ran her best race last time out when fourth behind a very promising filly from the Haggas yard; seems sure to win races this term but this might not be one of them unless she can take a step forward.
horses.breeding: ch f Sea The Stars - Anna Nerium

horses.spotlight_comment: Frankel filly; 15-2 for November's debut at Kempton (1m) where she kept on nicely once getting the hang of things in a race won by 1,000 Guineas entrant Abashiri; trainer is wasting no time in turning to headgear but brings potential into her second season.

Debut winner over 6f at Hamilton (good to soft); failed to justify a shade off odds-on when penalised at Southwell (7f AW) and that was disappointing, for all that a very slow pace might not have helped; bred to improve for this longer trip.

Half-sister to five winners; defied market weakness to go close in a 7f Kempton maiden in early April and was reportedly struck into when well held at Newbury (1m2f); this is no easy opportunity even with no excuses this time.

Quality 2yo form on all sorts of ground, as her seconds where behind smart horses and she wasn't beaten too far in a French Group 3; she did have the run of things up front on her Newmarket return (1m maiden, good) but was still unable to contain the less exposed So Regal; a 6lb pull with the winner could make it interesting.
horses.breeding: b f Mehmas - Maid To Remember

horses.spotlight_comment: Mehmas filly and the second foal out of a Group-placed 1m winner; bred to have a future but she'd need to be decidedly useful to take this on debut.

Top-class pedigree and holds a Coronation Stakes entry; clear promise on debut and again went off market leader when making no mistake in a 1m maiden at Newmarket's Craven meeting (good), emerging from off the pace to quicken past Lyrics Of Life under no more than hands and heels encouragement from Ryan Moore; penalised accordingly but she's highly promising.

5.30.betting_forecast: 7/2 Saytarr, 4/1 Colombier, Dosman, 7/1 Angel Hunter, Tilted Kilt, 8/1 Storm Star, 10/1 Greek Order, 12/1 Dingle, 25/1
5.30.spotlight_verdict: It's unlikely this race will throw up another My Cloud, who won 12 months ago en route to winning the Royal Hunt Cup. Colombier did have Group form in France but he's returning from a long absence and faces some in-form rivals. TILTED KILT won nicely on his AW reappearance and this different scenario won't faze him given he was runner-up in last year's always-competitive Silver Bowl at Haydock. Dosman is at the peak of his powers and he's second choice.[Alistair Jones]

horses.spotlight_comment: Behind Dosman at Southwell when tried in new blinkers two runs ago but left that form behind with a narrow verdict at Lingfield (1m), which seemed unlikely from where he was turning in; only 3lb higher and he's a C&D winner.

Won four times in France (7f-1m2f), twice in the Juddmonte silks and twice in these; absent since finishing ninth in Qatar in early 2025 so his wellbeing is a complete guessing game; best to let the betting guide; has form on soft and fast ground.
Effective in the reapplied cheekpieces but last season's career-best form came once fitted in a visor; needs to be right on his game to win this and that wasn't the case on his Newmarket comeback.
horses.breeding: b g Dandy Man - Sea Of Dreams

horses.spotlight_comment: Had the run of things when winning over Newcastle's 1m in January and has since finished behind both Dosman and Angel Hunter; goes to work today off his 8lb lower turf mark but that's because he's 0-15 on grass.

Only 2-16 but his third trainer has him in career-best form and didn't get the breaks when a closing fourth at Newcastle last time (1m); hold-up performer who needs a good pace to chase and if getting one he'll be dangerous.

Made the frame in three successive quality 1m handicaps last summer, including the Royal Hunt Cup here (good to firm); however, that campaign rather petered out and he was only midfield in the Lincoln a month ago (tried a visor); he's still dangerous to dismiss off this mark in a lower grade.

Tailed off in two races since winning off 7lb lower at Newbury last August (1m; in first-time cheekpieces which are now absent); might be high enough in the ratings even if all the better for being gelded; absent since October.

Won three handicaps on the AW in January 2025 (1m-1m2f) and showed that he's still on a fair mark with a second at Kempton on final run this January; however, this is tougher than he's accustomed to and has to prove himself on turf.
horses.breeding: b g Dark Angel - Elusive Beauty

horses.spotlight_comment: Five AW wins include this year's hat-trick on the Tapeta; raised a further 4lb for what was a narrow latest success (1m) but he's on a roll and no doubt a better horse now than when last seen on turf.

All four wins have been on the AW at Newcastle, including a hat-trick early last year; back on his last winning mark and he did chase a strong pace last time (in a race he won 12 months earlier) before folding late on; lightly raced on turf.
horses.breeding: ch g Night Of Thunder - Dancing Star

horses.spotlight_comment: Went 0-14 after his winning debut at two but belatedly doubled his tally when comfortably accounting for his five rivals after a break at Southwell (1m); this is tougher, but he was runner-up in last year's Silver Bowl at Haydock which was a Class 2 handicap on turf; only 3lb higher than that day.
